title: Resume a sorted SDDC Manager domain inventory after token expiry
prompt:
Implement `vcf_domain_snapshot/client.py` as a standard-library-only VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager integration. The inventory job's access token expires after an earlier page has already succeeded. Refresh the access token and resume the interrupted request without losing, duplicating, or refetching completed work.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a task-scoped projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the exact commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It was derived from that OpenAPI specification, not a rendered documentation page. The only operationIds in scope are `createToken`, `refreshAccessToken`, and `getDomains`; do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

Keep the public exports declared by `vcf_domain_snapshot/__init__.py`:

- `SddcManagerClient(base_url, username, password, *, timeout=10.0)` uses only Python standard-library `urllib` and `json` for transport. Treat `base_url` as an HTTP(S) origin: reject embedded credentials, a query, a fragment, or a non-root path. Disable environment proxies and redirects. Validate non-empty string credentials and a positive finite timeout locally. Every local argument rejection (invalid `base_url`, credentials, timeout, or page size) raises `ValueError` before any traffic.
- `SddcManagerClient.list_domains(*, page_size=2) -> list[dict]` returns the complete Domain collection, not page wrappers. Reject booleans and non-positive or non-int32 page sizes before any traffic.
- `SddcManagerError` represents HTTP and transport failures and exposes `.operation_id`, `.status_code`, and decoded JSON `.payload` when available. `ProtocolError` represents malformed success JSON or inconsistent pagination. Exception text and repr must never reveal the username, password, access token, refresh-token ID, response body, or underlying transport exception text.

Authenticate lazily once with `createToken`. Send compact UTF-8 JSON containing exactly `username` and `password`; omit the unset `apiKey` and `idToken` properties completely. Require a JSON object with a non-empty string `accessToken` and non-empty string `refreshToken.id`. Token creation has no Authorization header.

Retrieve zero-based `getDomains` pages beginning at page 0. Every GET must send exactly `pageNumber` followed by `pageSize` in the query, plus `Accept: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <current access token>`. It must have no request body or Content-Type. Do not invent or send any of the other optional query parameters in the contract.

Validate every successful page before using it. It must be a JSON object with an `elements` list of objects and a `pageMetadata` object. `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `totalElements`, and `totalPages` must be non-boolean, non-negative int32 values; the returned page number must match the request, `pageSize` must equal the number of returned elements, and totals must remain consistent. Reject an impossible page number, an overshoot, a non-progressing page before completion, or a final element count different from `totalElements`. Raise `ProtocolError` rather than returning a partial collection.

The fixture returns HTTP 401 on page 1 after page 0 succeeded. On the first 401 from `getDomains` only, call `refreshAccessToken` exactly once. Send the saved `refreshToken.id` as a compact JSON string with `Accept: application/json` and `Content-Type: application/json`, but no Authorization header. Require exactly HTTP 200 containing a non-empty JSON string, replace the access token, and retry only the failed page once. Do not call `createToken` again, restart pagination, refetch page 0, append the failed response, or append the retried page twice. A second 401 or any refresh failure is terminal.

After all pages validate, return every intact Domain dictionary in deterministic ascending order by case-folded string `name`, then ordinal string `id`, then canonical compact JSON as a tie-breaker. A missing or non-string name or id sorts as an empty string. Do not rely on response order: the protected mock flips element order on every successful collection response.

Use exactly the success status recorded for each operation. Requests with JSON bodies send `Content-Type: application/json`; every operation sends `Accept: application/json`. Do not retry any failure except the single interrupted `getDomains` request described above.

Run `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts the supplied contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates credentials and tokens at runtime, and reads its JSONL request log. It checks the exact method, target, headers, compact bodies, operation order, one-time refresh, same-page retry, preservation of completed work, optional-query omission, pagination validation, and deterministic sorting. The mock serves only the three operationIds named by the contract. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `.moonshiner/verify.py`, `docs/`, `tools/`, and `vcf_domain_snapshot/__init__.py` are protected; edit only `vcf_domain_snapshot/client.py`.
